correctness.rationale: Exact 36-cell enumeration and 3054-face coverage; 1402 disjoint Morse pairs and acyclicity verified on every one of 10368 Hasse incidences; 49-by-200 signed Morse attaching matrix has 37 unit pivots and zero residual 12-by-163 matrix. With one zero-cell and no one-cells, pi2 of the 49-sphere two-skeleton is free and integral row/column basis changes model the attaching maps, yielding the 12S2 plus 163S3 wedge. Independent original mod-two boundary ranks (35,325,863,216) corroborate.

evidence: The complex is a rainbow-matching complex of the properly edge-colored K6,6 given by S3 multiplication. Equivalently it is the matching complex of a three-partite 3-uniform Latin-square hypergraph with 36 hyperedges, or the independence complex of its hyperedge-intersection graph.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: These are isomorphic formulations of the same incidence rule, so same-object homotopy work under any of these names would dominate. Targeted searches revealed no exact S3 sphere-wedge classification; absence in search results is not proof of absolute novelty.

originality.rationale: Exact-object and equivalent-object literature searches did not find an implication covering the complete S3 partial-transversal homotopy classification. Paige (1951), Wanless (2002, 2007) study existence, while Hämäläinen (2009) has a different trades-vertex complex. A known cyclic order-six comparison does not determine the nonabelian case; risk of unindexed equivalent work remains.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently titled equivalent classification under hypergraph matching, rainbow-matching or Latin-square terminology cannot be excluded.
The 2002 Wanless full text was not materially inspected beyond official abstract; a hidden homotopy calculation is considered unlikely but not ruled out solely by that abstract.
The 2021 maximal-partial-transversal article was not read in entirety; inspected theorem statements concern length spectra rather than attaching maps.
The digital semantic index does not exhaust all private or older sources; scientific novelty is best-knowledge, not a uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: The nonabelian S3 table is the canonical smallest noncommutative group Latin square. Classical complete-mapping obstruction says no six-cell transversal but does not determine the complete topology of all partial transversals. The natural nonpure complex has a nontrivial mixed-dimensional integral wedge decomposition, distinct from the cyclic group of the same order and useful in exact comparisons of rainbow/3-uniform-hypergraph matching complexes. No broader generalization is claimed.
